outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) The agent provided three responsibilities even though only two were requested—extra info is not harmful. (2) Minor phrasing differences like “work-site arrangement” vs “Work site” label are inconsequential.

Critical issues: The agent did not provide the required “two preferred qualifications.” This is a hard requirement and part of the explicit stopping condition (“Stop after … recording … two preferred qualifications”). The screenshots support that the agent correctly searched Microsoft Careers for “Applied Scientist” in “Redmond, Washington,” opened a relevant listing (“Applied Scientist II / Senior Applied Scientist - Responsible AI (CoreAI)”) associated with “United States, Washington, Redmond + 4 more,” and correctly reported the job number (200017828), the work-site arrangement (“3 days / week in-office”), and at least two responsibilities that are visibly present in the Responsibilities section. The constraints were respected (no sign-in, no apply, no form submission).

However, despite achieving most elements, the task’s primary deliverable is the complete set of requested fields from the opened listing, and the agent explicitly failed to extract/report any preferred-qualification bullets. There is no screenshot evidence confirming the preferred qualifications content, and the agent’s output does not supply two items; thus the user does not receive the full required information from the listing. From an average user’s perspective, this is not a successful completion because a key requested component is missing rather than a minor formatting issue.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to use Microsoft Careers to find and open a relevant Applied Scientist listing associated with Redmond, WA, then report four specific pieces of information from that single listing: job number, work-site arrangement, two responsibilities, and two preferred qualifications—without signing in, applying, or submitting forms. The user would be flexible on which specific Applied Scientist listing is chosen (as long as it’s relevant and Redmond-associated), but not flexible on missing any of the required reported fields, especially the two preferred qualifications.
